newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN reports intimidation of minorities in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: UN reports intimidation of minorities in Bosnia.

text.p: A United Nations panel said on Thursday that minorities in post-war Bosnia were suffering "unchecked intimidation" and movement between different parts of the divided country remained severely limited.

Bosnian Serbs are the target of threats in the Sarajevo region while Moslems face intimidation both in the Serb Republic and in Bosnian-Croat controlled areas in the west, according to a report by U.N. monitors released in Geneva.

"Freedom of movement, expression and association remain severely restricted, returns of refugees and displaced persons to their former homes have been few, and personal security is under constant threat," said the U.N. human rights field operation in former Yugoslavia, which has 10 staff in Bosnia.
"On the critical issue of the right of refugees and displaced persons to return to their homes, little progress has taken place in the last month.
"Local minorities suffer under unchecked atmospheres of intimidation through the country," it added.
The report said a "systematic campaign of harassment" against 2,000 Bosnians in the town of Teslic in the Serb Republic continued without effective intervention by police.

"Attacks with grenades and other explosives, incidents of arson, looting and other forms of intimidation increasingly raise the likelihood that remaining minority residents will flee rather than live under Republika Srpska authority," it said.
The report also cited evictions of Moslems by Croats in the divided southern city of Mostar, saying they had substantially increased local tensions.
On Tuesday, U.N. relief workers reported that the Bosnian Croat army was involved in a brutal campaign of expulsions against Moslems in the Croat-held sector of Mostar.

A spokesman in Sarajevo for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said some 18 evictions were reported in six weeks in west Mostar and members of the Croat militia (HVO) were implicated in the "ethnic cleansing".
